children: Shares of Netflix Inc. (NFLX) edged lower about 0.12% in overnight trading late Tuesday, reversing a day in the green after the company announced its purchase of Los Angeles-based Radford Studio Center, marking its first ownership of a major Los Angeles-area studio lot.
The streaming giant did not disclose the purchase price. The Los Angeles Times reported that the deal was valued at $380 million, citing a person familiar with the matter.
Radford is home to many classic TV shows, including ‘Seinfeld,’ ‘Gunsmoke,’ ‘The Mary Tyler Moore Show,’ and ‘That ‘70s Show,’ among others.
Radford Marks Netflix’s LA-Area Studio Lot

Netflix became a contender to buy the 55-acre site in Studio City last spring after Goldman Sachs formally assumed control of the property at a foreclosure auction on Tuesday before the deal could close.

This marks Netflix’s first major studio lot’s outright ownership in the Los Angeles area. The acquisition is likely to help the streaming giant potentially consolidate productions that were previously scattered across leased spaces like Sunset Studios and Raleigh Studios.

“There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California's film industry,” Netflix said in a statement.

“This city is home to us. We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make LA, California, and the entertainment industry so special,” it added.
Netflix’s Recent Acquisitions

Netflix also acquired Interpositive, a Budapest-based provider of visual content creation services in March, to improve its competitive stance.

However, another user said, “$NFLX still looking great for the next leg down.”
